correctness.rationale: The finite-cluster proof is a direct implication chain through the source: amenability gives a hyperfinite Bernoulli graphing; smooth finite-cluster quotienting preserves hyperfiniteness; planarity and local finiteness pass to the quotient; Proposition 3.5 gives a pmp quotient; Theorem 6.4 gives a measurable five-coloring; Corollary 3.6 transfers it to an fiid coloring. In the unique-infinite case the source explicitly restricts the quotient graphing to finite components and Proposition 3.5(3) returns a partial factor on all finite clusters. The infinite-cluster membership event is measurable and equivariant, so a fresh sixth color completes the factor and is automatically proper across every edge incident to that quotient vertex.

value.rationale: The result improves the source's general amenable factor-of-iid bound from seven colors to five throughout the finite-cluster planar regime and to six throughout the unique-infinite-cluster planar regime. It also moves the paper's general measurable planar theorem back into the random-map factor setting beyond the square grid, producing a class-level structural corollary rather than a one-graph parameter increment.
